Model drift occurs when the statistical properties of the input data change over time, leading to a decline in model performance. Detecting drift is vital because it allows data scientists and engineers to identify when a model's predictions may no longer be valid, prompting necessary actions to maintain performance. ## Retraining Triggers. * **Data Volume Triggers**: Monitor the volume of new data; if a significant amount of new data is collected, it may warrant retraining to incorporate this information. results.title: What are Triggers in SQL: How to Implement them - Education Nest
results.content: With the help of SQL triggers, developers can specify SQL operations that should be carried out automatically whenever a specific event occurs in the database. A trigger is a particular kind of stored SQL procedure that starts an action—or, more precisely, fires an action—when an event like an INSERT, DELETE, or UPDATE occurs. A trigger can also include INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE logic, which means that when a data alteration triggers it, it may also result in another data modification, which triggers another trigger. A nested trigger has its own data storage modification logic. Triggers are often referred to as “a particular sort of stored process.” Stored procedures are not event-driven or connected to a specific table, in contrast to triggers. Each trigger only functions when an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE event occurs and is specific to one table in the database. ●  **INSERT**: When a new row is added to the table, as happens when using the INSERT, LOAD DATA, and REPLACE statements, the trigger becomes active.
